A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NSNQuant work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original perplexity, generation, efficiency, and ablation results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds calibration controls, expanded Hadamard ablations, and detailed latency measurements.

M1.justification: The NSN transformations, Hadamard placement, scale adjustment, codebook tuning, double quantization, and residual-cache procedure are unchanged. The revised Figure 2 illustrates the existing method.

E1.justification: The new W16C16 condition broadens CQ calibration from WikiText-2 alone to a WikiText-2/C4 mixture (v2 Appendix C.7). The evaluation benchmark suite and task families, including AIME-2024, are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator algorithms are retained, including KIVI, KIVI + Hadamard, KVQuant, CQ, QuaRot, SpinQuant, and FP16. W32 and W16C16 change existing CQ baselines' calibration settings rather than introducing new comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: V2 adds 32-sample CQ calibration controls and a perplexity evaluation with 4096-token truncation for LCC/SAMSum in the Hadamard ablation. Latency profiling adds batch-size/prompt-length combinations of 4/4096 and 128/128 alongside the retained 32/512 configuration, with 64 generated tokens.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.7 tests whether increasing CQ calibration size or diversity improves generalization. Appendix C.1 extends the Hadamard-versus-RHT ablation to LCC and SAMSum. The existing latency analysis gains operation-level breakdowns and additional configurations.

E5.justification: Both versions report latency averaged over 100 runs and AIME-2024 evaluation with five seeds. V2 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds calibration-control and LCC/SAMSum ablation scores. For example, CQ-8c10b GSM8K accuracy is 46.47 with W16C16 versus 24.26 with original calibration. Reported NSNQuant-2b latency changes from 1.675 s prefill/32.4 ms decode in v1 Table 21 to 1707.22 ms/36.49 ms in v2 Table 5. The separate 1-bit latency row disappears; main benchmark and AIME scores are retained.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, its assumptions and proof, the attention-computation derivation, and the mathematical discussion of NSN variants are retained. Changes to notation and typesetting do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about calibration-free quantization, distribution alignment, low-bit generalization, and up to threefold throughput improvement.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new CQ controls as favoring calibration diversity over sample-count growth and acknowledges potential benefits and costs of further calibration. It explicitly identifies decode-heavy workloads as favorable for NSNQuant. Existing early-layer, inter-channel-dependency, and safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly identifies LLaMA2-7B for latency measurements and labels decoding latency as per-step. It documents calibration-mixture recipes and truncation settings for the added checks. Existing software and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The same 44 cited works and central positioning of calibration-free NSNQuant against calibration-dependent CQ are retained. Related Work moves from v1 Appendix J to v2 Section 5 with essentially the same substance.

P1.justification: Related Work moves into the main text, and the appendix latency discussion is reorganized into Section 4.6 and Appendix F.4. V2 also makes limited grammatical and terminology corrections and updates acknowledgements and the conference footer.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer legends and a token/channel schematic. The Hadamard table gains LCC/SAMSum columns, a CQ calibration table is added, and latency tables gain component and configuration breakdowns. Other figures are retained, with some relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The CQ calibration controls better test whether the reported generalization advantage depends on a small, homogeneous calibration set. Expanded timing breakdowns make computational overhead more transparent, and broader Hadamard ablations strengthen supporting evidence. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the separate 1-bit latency row; the method, theory, and central benchmark results remain unchanged.
